text:
Sam: quick question — saw a weird read-after-write on a tenant after a compaction run, want eyes
Maria: what happened? repro steps?
Sam: small repro — tenant does lots of short-lived prefixes; compaction ran, we compacted tombstones, then client did a write that should have been visible immediately but read path returned older value
Sam: looks like residency metadata for that prefix got compacted away and the handshake assumed residency still holds
Ashley: hmm. are you using lease epoch only or storing explicit residency generation in the slab header?
Sam: only epoch token + last_touch_time
Lee: that gap is scary. compaction removing ancillary residency tags could break the lease/lightweight handshake
Maria: can you paste the evict/compact log around the time? snippet is fine
Sam: sure
```
[compact] shard=7 tenant=acme prefix=abc123 compaction_start=2026-03-20T03:12:08Z
[compact] removed_tombstones=42 maybe_residency_tag=0x0
[lease] lease_revoke shard=7 prefix=abc123 epoch=4321 -> new_epoch=4322
[write] tenant=acme prefix=abc123 client_write=0xdeadbeef at=2026-03-20T03:12:09Z
```
Ashley: looks like compactor collapsed the metadata block that previously carried a residency bitset. after compaction the read path didn't see the residency marker and forwarded to a stale replica
Lee: one option: keep a compacted-residency sentinel in the key index that survives GC for N seconds after compaction
Ashley: sentinel might bloat index, though. we could instead include an explicit resid_generation in the lease token and verify on read
Maria: resid_generation in lease token sounds cleaner: increment on any compaction/handoff which changes physical placement. read checks token matches slab header generation
Sam: agree, but we need to ensure increment is cheap and never races with lease renewals
Lee: atomic swap during compaction: take local lock, increment generation, write generation delta in compaction tombstone, release. Handshake compares epoch+gen pair
Ashley: that is doable. we must update canary upgrade path: older nodes that haven't read the new generation should fallback to conservative behavior (force remote validation)
Maria: operationally, how long do we keep compatibility fallbacks? ASAP cutoff with rollout plan
Sam: quick perf question — will adding gen check add an extra RPC on cold reads? we can make it a local check most of the time, only fallback to RPC if mismatch
Lee: yes. mismatch path incurs RPC and that's our graceful degradation for mixed-version clusters
Ashley: from storage compaction side: add a tiny fixed-size header to compaction output with gen uint32. 8 bytes per compacted extent, negligible
Maria: can we sketch the API change for the lease token? e.g., token={epoch}:{gen} and handshake returns mismatch if token_gen != slab_gen
Sam: exactly. also update tracing metrics: lease.gen_mismatch_count, compact.gen_bump_count
Lee: propose: small spike to implement gen bump + read fallback. do a perf run on stressbed before rolling to prod
Sam: +1
Ashley: I'll do the compactor change (write gen bump tombstone) — need 2 days
Maria: i'll own the handshake change and canary rollout plan
Lee: i'll wire up metrics and stress tests
infra-bot: deploy scheduled: staging/compactor-gen-bump -> 2026-03-22 10:00 UTC :rocket:
Sam: thanks all — opened a quick RFC gist with the one-pager and steps, link: https://go/rfc/resid-gen-spike :memo:
Maria: added action items to triage board, assigning to @Ashley @Lee @Maria
Ashley: noted. will report back with benchmark numbers and a failing repro case turned into unit test
Sam: closing thread for now, will ping when staging results land :thumbsup:
